title: Project proposal
text: Question: Among adults aged 40 years older 2009–2012 NHANES data, BMI associated average systolic blood pressure? use NHANESraw R package NHANES (version 2.1.4), containing 20,293 participants 2009–2010 2011–2012 cycles. observation represents one participant. object retains survey-design variables differs package’s resampled NHANES object. packaged data intended educational use. exposure BMI kg/m², modeled continuously reported per 5-unit increase. outcome BPSysAve, average systolic blood pressure mmHg, continuous variable. target population adults aged 40+ civilian, noninstitutionalized US population covered NHANES, although missing data educational extract limit population inference. fitting models, specify adjustment age, sex, race/ethnicity (Race1), education, family income--poverty ratio (Poverty), survey cycle. Age sex relate body composition blood pressure. Socioeconomic circumstances social conditions can influence outcomes; race/ethnicity treated social-context variable, biological explanation. Cycle accounts differences survey periods. Age income--poverty ratio initially continuous; covariates categorical. extract contains 7,738 adults aged 40+, 7,060 BMI blood pressure observed. BMI missing 391, blood pressure 581, education 17, income--poverty ratio 790. 6,392 participants primary-model variables observed positive examination weights. describe missingness participant characteristics, plot BMI blood pressure, fit survey-weighted linear regression. construct design using strata (SDMVSTRA), clusters (SDMVPSU), four-year examination weights (WTMEC2YR / 2). define design participants positive examination weights subsetting analysis domain. Results include adjusted differences mmHg 95% confidence intervals. primary analysis use complete cases. compare included excluded participants examine sensitivity omitting income variable, including comparison sample. Residual plots nonlinear BMI term assess model form. Survey weights automatically correct item nonresponse. Cross-sectional measurement, unavailable treatment information, unmeasured confounding, age top-coding 80 limit interpretation. Results describe associations, causal effects.
